changes: pads: none → pads (groove_mm 0, lip_mm 0, pad_angle_deg 30, pad_tpu_mm 2, reach_mm 0, width_mm 12)
why: This is the cheap rung: $0, 0 days, 16 machine minutes, all on hand. Brief at 45 deg: 85 mm face +14 deg, tip +14 mm (vs +23 mm stock). I chose 30 deg as a compromise. It should bring gelatin (73 mm, top +15) and probably tuna (85 mm, top +17) and pudding (90 mm, top +19) under their tops with tolerable tilt on TPU, while keeping small objects closer to parallel than 45 deg would (at 45 deg, 35 mm is −21 deg with the tip −10 mm). The wider sugar box and mustard may still miss. I also expect this pad (TPU friction) to combine with the long_slide swap if both are kept, since they are in different slots.

An angle between the two, 38 deg, should put the tip at about +18 to +19 mm at 85 mm and lower as System 1 squeezes in. That could bring tuna's side under the pad while staying clear of the 45 deg collision that cost banana. Width 10 mm (from 12) trims the pad's early contact. It costs nothing, all items are on hand, and it is a fallback in case the slide's rack keeps hitting tomato.

This is the same interpolation step that worked before. 30→38 deg gained gelatin and tuna, and 45 deg lost banana. At 42 deg the face and tip at 90 mm come out close to what 38 deg gives at 85 mm: about 21 deg tilt and a tip of about +20 mm. That geometry already holds tuna_fish_can (85 mm, 34 tall, top +17, metal mu 0.35, 171 g). Pudding (90 mm, 38 tall, top +19, cardboard mu 0.5, 187 g) is a similar low, wide box with better friction, so it should hold the same way. Sugar (92 mm, top +23) gets about 22 deg and a tip of about +21 mm, so it may also come in. If the box is held properly, its load_limit stall should clear: 0.41 + 0.15 x 5.14 = 1.18 N*m < 1.62. Mustard (96 mm) is beyond the 94-95 mm opening, so no pad value reaches it. The cheaper move is the only one left: this costs $0 and 6 machine min, all on hand. The swap alternative, long_slide, lost tomato_soup_can in all six of its trials because its rack pressed on the can's top, so it is not repeated.

If 1 mm of skin isn't enough for pudding's top edge, the full 4 mm thickness step gives twice the angle shift. It still costs $0 and needs no purchase: the pads print in PLA only, which also saves the TPU print time. If friction is set by the lower of the two surfaces, nothing changes for the held objects. If it is set by a mix of the two, the 3–4× grip margin covers the loss.
